sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: revenue up 18%, core loss per share improved from ($1.13) to ($0.49), free cash flow usage improved from ($3.9B) to ($2.3B), and management describes a 'solid quarter' with 'recovery plan in full swing.' However, full-year free cash flow guidance was not formally raised (management says 'we're not going to adjust that full year range right now'), and significant risks remain from China tariffs (50 deliveries at risk) and input cost tariffs (less than $500M annual impact). The structural tariff risk and unchanged formal guidance prevent a higher score.

summary.revenue: $19.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year, primarily driven by higher commercial delivery volume.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.16); core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($0.49), improved from ($1.13) in the prior year.
summary.guidance: Full-year free cash flow guidance not adjusted; management expects second half free cash flow to turn positive and accelerate. 737 production expected to reach 38 per month over the next few months, 787 to 7 per month. China delivery plan of ~50 airplanes for the year is at risk due to tariffs, but management expects to largely offset any cash flow impact.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin of 2.4% (up from -0.5% in 1Q24); core operating margin of 1.0% (up from -2.3%). Commercial Airplanes operating margin of -6.6% (improved from -24.6%). Defense, Space & Security operating margin of 2.5% (up from 2.2%). Global Services operating margin of 18.6% (up from 18.2%).
key_risks: China tariffs: approximately 50 China deliveries at risk; customers have indicated they will not take delivery.
Input cost tariffs: net annual impact less than $500 million, with potential supply chain continuity issues.
Seat certification issues affecting some deliveries expected to be a challenge for the balance of the year.
Structural risk from ongoing certification programs (737-7, 737-10, 777X) with no change to previously shared timelines.
Potential retaliatory tariffs beyond China could affect ability to deliver aircraft.
Fixed-price development programs in Defense (15% of revenue) still require risk retirement.
key_opportunities: F-47 win: selected by U.S. Air Force to design, build and deliver next-generation fighter, securing fighter franchise for decades.
Production rate increases: 737 to 38/month (and eventually 42, 47, 52), 787 to 7/month (and eventually double-digit rates).
Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture for $10.55 billion provides significant cash infusion and strengthens balance sheet.
Strong demand: backlog of $545 billion, key commercial programs sold out into next decade.
Improved operational performance: 50% reduction in traveled work, 25% reduction in rework hours on 737 line.
Duty drawback opportunity: ability to recover tariff costs on exported aircraft (80% of deliveries).

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Kelly Ortberg stated 'our recovery plan is in full swing and showing signs that it's being effective' and 'I feel really good about our overall plan for the year,' reflecting a confident tone despite acknowledged risks.

evidence.claim: Revenue was $19.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year.
evidence.quote: Revenue was $19.5 billion, up 18%, primarily driven by higher commercial delivery volume.

evidence.claim: Core loss per share improved from ($1.13) to ($0.49).
evidence.quote: Core loss per share of $0.49 was a significant improvement compared to last year, driven by higher commercial deliveries and improved operational performance across the business.

evidence.claim: Free cash flow usage improved from ($3.9B) to ($2.3B).
evidence.quote: Free cash flow was a usage of $2.3 billion in the quarter, reflecting higher commercial deliveries and a working capital usage that improved compared to both the prior year and quarter.

evidence.claim: Full-year free cash flow guidance was not adjusted.
evidence.quote: In terms of the range that you mentioned, we're not going to adjust that full year range right now. We're good with where it's at.

evidence.claim: China tariffs put approximately 50 deliveries at risk.
evidence.quote: We have approximately 50 China deliveries in our plan for the balance of the year. We are in close communication with our China customers and we're actively assessing options for remarketing already built or in-process airplanes.

evidence.claim: Input cost tariffs net annual impact is less than $500 million.
evidence.quote: On the supply chain side, the net annual impact of higher tariffs on our input costs is manageable. And within our plan, it's less than $500 million annually.

evidence.claim: GAAP operating margin improved to 2.4% from -0.5%.
evidence.quote: Operating margins (GAAP) 2.4 % (0.5) %

evidence.claim: Commercial Airplanes operating margin improved to -6.6% from -24.6%.
evidence.quote: Operating margins (24.6)% (6.6)% 1Q24 1Q25

evidence.claim: Defense, Space & Security operating margin improved to 2.5% from 2.2%.
evidence.quote: Operating margins 2.2 % 2.5 % 1Q24 1Q25

evidence.claim: Global Services operating margin improved to 18.6% from 18.2%.
evidence.quote: Operating margins 18.2 % 18.6 % 1Q24 1Q25

evidence.claim: Management tone is confident.
evidence.quote: Our recovery plan is in full swing and showing signs that it's being effective.

evidence.claim: F-47 win secures fighter franchise for decades.
evidence.quote: To be selected the contractor for the world's first sixth-generation fighter is a testament to our focused investment in some pretty difficult time and to our dedicated team. This will secure our fighter franchise for decades to come.

evidence.claim: Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture for $10.55 billion provides significant cash infusion.
evidence.quote: As you saw yesterday, we entered into an agreement to sell portions of our Digital Aviation Solutions business for $10.55 billion, which is an important component of our strategy to focus on our core businesses and strengthen the balance sheet.

evidence.claim: Backlog is $545 billion.
evidence.quote: Total company backlog at quarter end was $545 billion.

evidence.claim: 50% reduction in traveled work and 25% reduction in rework hours on 737 line.
evidence.quote: If you look back before the strike last fall, we've seen about a 50% reduction in traveled work and a 25% reduction in rework hours on the 737 line.

evidence.claim: Seat certification issues expected to be a challenge for the balance of the year.
evidence.quote: As we highlighted last quarter, we continue to work through seat certification issues affecting some deliveries, and I expect this will be a challenge for us for the balance of the year.

evidence.claim: 737 production expected to reach 38 per month over the next few months.
evidence.quote: We are currently producing in the low 30s per month and expect that we'll get to the 38 per month cap over the next few months.

evidence.claim: 787 production expected to increase to 7 per month this year.
evidence.quote: We're poised to move to seven per month this year, provided our KPIs indicate a stable production system and they're currently looking very good.

evidence.claim: Duty drawback opportunity exists for exported aircraft.
evidence.quote: We do have suppliers in countries subject to the new US tariffs, most notably in Japan and Italy, where our suppliers do significant structures work on our wide-body airplanes. We are currently paying the 10% tariff on those components, but we should recover tariff costs for those aircraft that are subsequently exported, which is a large portion of our wide-bodies.

evidence.claim: Potential retaliatory tariffs beyond China could affect deliveries.
evidence.quote: The other issue is impact of potential retaliatory tariffs from other countries, which could affect our ability to deliver aircraft.

review_flags.reason: The score of 0.20 is based on genuine operational momentum and confident management tone, but the lack of a formal guidance raise and the presence of structural tariff risks could justify a slightly lower score. A human reviewer should confirm the balance between positive operational trends and unresolved risks.
